name: Vitamin C for gums
lead: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is used or proposed for gum health, in the context of scurvy-related gum bleeding and, in recent dental trials, for gingival pigmentation treatments.[1]

Scurvy, caused by inadequate vitamin C, includes gum disease and loosening teeth among its signs, and vitamin C is needed for collagen synthesis.[1] Beyond scurvy, general reference sources do not establish an effect on ordinary gum disease. Several registered trials have studied vitamin C applied by microneedling or injection to treat dark gum pigmentation.[2][3]
infobox: Dietary supplement; investigational in dental procedures

paras: Scurvy gum changes resolve with vitamin C treatment, and symptoms usually take at least a month of little or no intake to appear.[1] Historical accounts describe gum overgrowth in sailors.[1]

Registered trials compare vitamin C delivered by microneedling, injection or mesotherapy with other approaches such as diode laser for gingival melanin pigmentation.[2][3] One trial examines vitamin C as an adjunct for pigment recurrence.[4] Results were not found for most of these.

Registered studies include a completed trial of vitamin C mesotherapy versus diode laser for physiologic gingival pigmentation[3] and recruiting or unknown-status trials of microneedling with vitamin C.[2][4][5] Results from these were not available to this article. A registered trial also explores vitamin C and orthodontic relapse.[6]

timeline.event: James Lind trial showed citrus fruit could treat scurvy.[1]
Link between hexuronic acid and scurvy established; later named ascorbic acid.[1]

card.summary: Vitamin C reverses scurvy gum bleeding; dental trials of gum depigmentation are ongoing with little published.
card.note: Benefit shown for deficiency; effects in healthy gums are not established.

quick.overview:
Vitamin C is needed to make collagen, and severe deficiency (scurvy) causes bleeding, swollen gums and loose teeth. Those signs resolve when vitamin C is restored.

In dentistry, small registered trials test vitamin C applied to lighten dark gum pigmentation.
quick.mechanism: Vitamin C supports collagen formation, which maintains blood vessels and connective tissue.
quick.risks: Dietary vitamin C is generally well tolerated. The dental techniques in trials are investigational.
